quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When driving on snow or ice, what should you do?

options.text: It is safe to use your cruise control.
Change your speed and direction slowly and gradually.
Drive the same way you would on dry roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your speed and direction slowly and gradually.
questions.explanation: On snow or ice, make all speed and direction changes slowly. Never use cruise control on snow or ice because your tires may lose grip and you could lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: What does this red and white sign tell you to do?

options.text: Stop and look both ways before driving.
Let other traffic go first before you enter or cross.
Keep your speed steady and watch all directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other traffic go first before you enter or cross.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means you must slow down and be ready to stop so other vehicles, cyclists, or pedestrians can pass first. You do not have the right-of-way.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, what must you do?

options.text: Watch for vehicles that must stop at railroad crossings, like school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials.
Watch for trains coming from both directions.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with caution. Only cross when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. Watch for vehicles that must stop at crossings, such as school buses and hazardous material trucks.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is correct?

options.text: Side mirrors eliminate all blind spots.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
You can see blind spots in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Large trucks have much bigger blind spots than regular cars, and drivers should avoid these areas.

questions.question: If you drive slower than other traffic, what will likely happen?

options.text: You will block traffic and could get a ticket.
You will improve traffic flow.
You will show safe driving skills.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will block traffic and could get a ticket.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly and blocking the normal flow of traffic can result in a ticket. You should match the speed of traffic, unless traffic is going over the speed limit.

questions.question: What does this black and yellow sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right is one-way traffic only.
There is a detour to the right because of road construction.
The road ahead turns at a sharp angle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns at a sharp angle.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They warn you about conditions ahead. This sign tells you to slow down for a sharp turn in the road.

questions.question: When are collisions most likely to happen?

options.text: When all vehicles travel at about the same speed.
When one lane travels faster than other lanes.
When one vehicle travels faster or slower than other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: When one vehicle travels faster or slower than other traffic.
questions.explanation: Collisions happen more often when one driver goes faster or slower than other vehicles. Driving faster than traffic increases crash risk. Driving slower causes rear-end collisions or forces other drivers to swerve.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines between traffic lanes mean?

options.text: You can pass from the left.
You can pass from the right.
You cannot pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Double solid lines mean no passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.question: What danger does fatigue increase?

options.text: Missing an exit.
Being late to an appointment.
Falling asleep while driving and crashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Falling asleep while driving and crashing.
questions.explanation: Fatigue slows your thinking and judgment. You may fall asleep behind the wheel and crash, which can injure or kill you or others.

questions.question: When you see flashing red lights at a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Drive faster than the approaching train.
Stop completely.
Find a way around the lowered gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing signs warn of approaching trains. You must obey all railroad warning signs and lights. Never try to go around barriers.

questions.question: A driver ahead of you stops at a crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Pass the vehicle slowly at 10 mph or less.
Stop and wait until all pedestrians have crossed.
Change lanes, look carefully, and pass the stopped vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until all pedestrians have crossed.
questions.explanation: Never pass a stopped vehicle at a crosswalk. Pedestrians may be crossing where you cannot see them. Stop and proceed only after all pedestrians have finished crossing.

questions.question: If you drive faster than other vehicles on a two-lane road and pass cars repeatedly, you will:

options.text: Get to your destination much faster and more safely.
Increase your risk of a collision.
Help reduce traffic jams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your risk of a collision.
questions.explanation: Avoid passing other vehicles on two-lane roads. Each time you pass another car, your collision risk goes up.

questions.question: Only ____ can lower blood alcohol content (BAC) and reduce alcohol's effects on your body.

options.text: Drinking caffeine
Eating fatty foods
Time

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time can remove alcohol and its effects from your body.

questions.question: You have stopped at a railroad crossing for a train. After the train passes, you should:

options.text: Wait for all warning lights to stop flashing.
Watch for a second train.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: After a train passes, watch for a second train on any track. Do not move until all gates are raised and all warning lights have stopped flashing.

questions.question: If you have a tire blowout:

options.text: Tap or pump the brakes.
Slow down gradually and use light braking.
Press the brakes hard and fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and use light braking.
questions.explanation: If you have a tire blowout, slow down by easing off the accelerator. Do not brake hard until the vehicle has slowed down a lot.

questions.question: When driving on gravel or dirt roads:

options.text: Your tires grip better than on pavement.
Your tires have less grip than on pavement, so you must slow down.
You can see better than on pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires have less grip than on pavement, so you must slow down.
questions.explanation: Tires grip loose gravel and dirt less than they grip concrete and asphalt. On gravel or dirt roads, slow down. Your stopping distance is longer and you can skid more easily when turning.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?

options.text: Alertness and focus.
Reaction time and coordination.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows down the nervous system. It reduces alertness, cuts your ability to focus, slows your reaction time, and severely impacts your coordination.

questions.question: Which statement about large trucks is true?

options.text: They take longer to stop than regular vehicles.
They all have air brakes that let them stop quickly.
They are easier to steer than regular vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They take longer to stop than regular vehicles.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop than other vehicles at the same speed. A regular vehicle at 55 mph stops in about 400 feet. A large truck at the same speed needs almost 800 feet to stop.

questions.question: Which of these slows down traffic flow?

options.text: Slowing down to look at a crash.
Not changing lanes unless necessary.
Using public transportation instead of driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down to look at a crash.
questions.explanation: Slowing down to look at crashes causes traffic jams and should be avoided.

questions.question: When you see someone crossing the street with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Stop until the person is completely out of your way.
Honk your horn as you drive past them.
Drive carefully around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the person is completely out of your way.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind person crossing the street with a white cane or guide dog, you must stop until they are well away from your vehicle. Always give blind pedestrians the right-of-way.

questions.question: You must use low beams when you are:

options.text: On a lighted street.
On a freeway.
In fog.

questions.correctAnswerText: In fog.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off water and create glare, making it harder to see. Some cars have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Assume all drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Always be ready to yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Do not assume you have the right-of-way. Always look at the situation at an intersection. Yield your right-of-way if it prevents a crash.

questions.question: If you get tired while driving, the best thing to do is:

options.text: Stop to rest or let someone else drive.
Drink coffee.
Open a window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to rest or let someone else drive.
questions.explanation: Stop to rest or change drivers if you feel tired. Tiredness slows your mind and reactions, making driving unsafe.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines in the center of a road mean passing is:

options.text: Allowed from both directions.
Allowed only from your direction.
Not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double yellow lines mean no one can cross the center line to pass from either direction.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Anything that causes sudden steering while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving means anything that takes your eyes, hands, or mind off the road. It is the leading cause of crashes. Distractions cause drivers to miss important sights and sounds needed to avoid crashes.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, it is safe to return to your lane if you:

options.text: Cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.
See the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
Have passed the other vehicle's front bumper.

questions.correctAnswerText: See the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Make sure you are far enough ahead before returning to your lane. When you see both headlights in your rearview mirror, you have enough space to return safely.

questions.question: A solid yellow arrow on a traffic light means:

options.text: Speed up to make the turn before the light changes.
You do not need to signal your turn.
Get ready to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get ready to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the green arrow is ending. Prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic before turning.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: School crossing.
School zone.
Pedestrian crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a crosswalk. Watch for people crossing the road.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No U-turn.
Traffic signal ahead.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign says U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Intersection ahead.
Merging traffic.
Steep hill ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns of a steep hill ahead. Slow down to avoid crashes and brake damage.

questions.question: A school bus ahead has its lights flashing and signal arm extended. What should you do?

options.text: Stop.
Go 15 mph if you don't see children.
Go at normal speed, but watch for children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: You must stop completely when a school bus has flashing lights and an extended arm. Stay stopped until the arm retracts and the bus moves. This rule applies whether you are behind the bus or coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: In a crash, what should you do with injured people?

options.text: Move them far from the road.
Don't move them unless absolutely necessary.
Tell them they don't need medical help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't move them unless absolutely necessary.
questions.explanation: Moving injured people can cause more harm. Only move someone if there is immediate danger like fire. Keep injured people sitting or lying down until medical help arrives.

questions.question: Before you change lanes, you should check your mirrors and:

options.text: Never look over your right shoulder.
Always slow down in your lane.
Look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Always look over your shoulder before changing lanes. This helps you see vehicles in the lane you want to enter. Check that no other drivers are moving into the same spot.

questions.question: You see animals standing near the road. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.
Slow down and drive carefully.
Quickly swerve to the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and drive carefully.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be careful around animals near the road. They may suddenly move into traffic. There may also be other animals hidden from view.

questions.question: You may legally block an intersection:

options.text: If you entered on a green light.
During rush hour.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never block an intersection. Even if the light is green, only enter if you can completely cross before the light turns red. You can get a ticket for blocking an intersection.

questions.question: A school bus on your side of the road has red lights flashing. What must you do?

options.text: Slow to 10 mph or less.
Stop until the lights stop flashing.
Change lanes and pass carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights and a stop arm mean the bus is picking up or dropping off students. You must stay stopped until the lights stop flashing and the arm goes back in. Never pass a bus that is loading or unloading students.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Jogging trail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign shows a crosswalk, whether it's marked on the pavement or not. Watch for pedestrians and let them cross safely.

questions.question: In rain or fog, drivers should use their:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in rain, snow, sleet, or fog. High beams reflect off the precipitation and bounce back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: This bicyclist is signaling:

options.text: A left turn.
A stop.
A right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: A left turn.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists use hand signals because they don't have turn signals. A left arm stretched straight out means the bicyclist is turning left.

questions.question: A broken yellow line down the center of the road means:

options.text: Construction is ahead.
No one can pass.
Anyone can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anyone can pass when safe.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on a two-lane road means any driver can pass when there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: You see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Keep going. You have the right-of-way.
Stop and wait for the pedestrians to cross.
Turn right and go around the pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait for the pedestrians to cross.
questions.explanation: Drivers must let pedestrians cross at crosswalks. Wait until the crosswalk is clear before you drive through.

questions.question: Before entering an intersection, you should look:

options.text: Left, right, then left again.
Right.
Left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left, right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look both left and right for cars and pedestrians. Look left again because vehicles from your left will reach you first. Check the whole intersection to make sure it is clear before moving.

questions.question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is true?

options.text: If you can walk straight after drinking, it is safe to drive.
Driving is safe if you are below the legal alcohol limit.
Alcohol impairs your judgment, which you need to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol impairs your judgment, which you need to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects your judgment. You need good judgment to react safely to road conditions. Any amount of alcohol can impair your driving, even if you are below the legal limit.

questions.question: At a crosswalk:

options.text: You must yield to pedestrians.
Pedestrians must yield to you.
Construction workers must yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crosswalks. Drivers must stop for pedestrians, whether the crosswalk is marked or not.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Falling rocks
Trucks use second gear
Steep hill ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep hill ahead
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you a steep hill is coming. Slow down and shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: To check your blind spot when changing lanes:

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Use your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Mirrors cannot show your blind spots. Always turn your head and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.

questions.question: As you drive faster, it is important to:

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Look far ahead of your vehicle.
Change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: At higher speeds, your car needs more distance to stop. Look far ahead so you have time to react safely to hazards.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Watch for bicycles.
Bicycles are not allowed.
Bicycle repair shop ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for bicycles.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts you that bicycles may be crossing the road. Be ready to slow down or stop.

questions.question: Should you always drive slower than other traffic?

options.text: No, driving too slowly blocks traffic.
Yes, it is a good defensive driving technique.
Yes, it is always safer.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, driving too slowly blocks traffic.
questions.explanation: Drive slowly in heavy traffic or bad weather. But if you drive too slowly and block traffic flow, you can get a ticket.

questions.question: If you park in an unusual spot:

options.text: Keep your reverse lights on.
Make sure drivers can see your vehicle from all directions.
Park five feet from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure drivers can see your vehicle from all directions.
questions.explanation: Your parked car must be visible to all approaching drivers. This prevents accidents and keeps your car safe.
